aspects.says: Bit 65 announces a tertiary bitmap the way bit 1 announces the secondary one, so field 65 carries no data.
basis: section:2.3. Bit 1 Announces a Second Bitmap, So It Is Never a Field

aspects.says: Bit 1 announces a secondary bitmap for fields 65 to 128, which comes before the first field; bit 1 itself is not a field.
basis: section:2.3. Bit 1 Announces a Second Bitmap, So It Is Never a Field

aspects.says: The same 64 bits travel as 8 bytes or 16 hexadecimal characters, as each link's specification says, and the bytes don't tell which.
basis: section:2.4. The Same Bits Travel as 8 Bytes or as 16 Characters

aspects.says: Bit n of a bitmap says field n is present, counted from 1 at the most significant bit of the first byte.
basis: section:2.2. Bit n Says Field n Is Present, Counted From 1 at the Leftmost Bit

aspects.says: A message whose highest field is 64 has one bitmap; any field above 64 brings the secondary bitmap.

aspects.says: A response changes the MTI's third digit and a repeat its fourth, and a repeat is answered like the original.

aspects.says: A receiver trusts the bitmap, so a bitmap off by one bit reads every field with another field's definition and may still unpack.
